weeks.topic: Compter de 0 à 20 (Counting from 0 to 20) - Part 1  zéro (0), un (1), deux (2), trois (3),
weeks.content:
 Numbers 0-10 review and practice:
quatre (4), cinq (5), six (6), sept (7), huit
(8), neuf (9), dix (10)
 Pronunciation practice for each number
 Counting objects in classroom
 Simple math in French: deux plus trois
égale cinq (2 + 3 = 5)
 Number songs and rhymes

weeks.topic: Compter de 0 à 20 (Counting from 0 to 20) - Part 2  onze (11), douze (12), treize (13),
weeks.content:
 Numbers 11-20:
quatorze (14), quinze (15), seize (16),
dix-sept (17), dix-huit (18), dix-neuf
(19), vingt (20)
 Counting from 0 to 20 fluently
 Asking "Combien?" (How many?):
Combien de livres? (How many books?)
 Using numbers in context: J'ai quinze
ans (I am 15 years old), Il y a dix élèves
(There are 10 students)
 Number games: counting relay, number
bingo

 Introduction to time vocabulary:
- L'heure (time/hour), Quelle
heure est-il? (What time is it?)
- Il est... heures (It is... o'clock)
 Telling time on the hour: Il est une
heure (It's 1 o'clock), Il est deux heures
(It's 2 o'clock), etc.
 Parts of the day: le matin (morning),
l'après-midi (afternoon), le soir
(evening), la nuit (night)
 Simple time statements: Il est huit
heures du matin (It's 8 o'clock in the
morning)

 Telling time with half hours and
quarters:
- Et demie (half past): Il est deux
heures et demie (It's 2:30)
- Et quart (quarter past): Il est
trois heures et quart (It's 3:15)
- Moins le quart (quarter to): Il est
quatre heures moins le quart (It's
3:45)
 Asking and telling time in dialogues
 Daily routines with time: Je me réveille
à sept heures (I wake up at 7 o'clock)
 Creating daily schedules in French

weeks.content:
 Meals vocabulary:
(dinner)

Boire (to drink)
 Common foods:
- Le pain (bread), Le riz (rice), La
viande (meat), Le poisson (fish)
- Les fruits (fruits): la banane
(banana), l'orange (orange), la

weeks.topic: Identifier les aliments et les repas (Identifying Foods and Meals) - - Drinks: l'eau (water), le jus Part 2 (juice), le lait (milk), le thé (tea)
weeks.content:
 More food vocabulary:
- Other foods: les œufs (eggs), le
fromage (cheese), le gâteau

- Nigerian foods in French: le
garri, le fufu, le jollof rice
 Expressing likes and dislikes: J'aime...
(I like...), Je n'aime pas... (I don't like...)
 Meal times: Je prends le petit-déjeuner
à sept heures (I have breakfast at 7
o'clock)
 Food-related verbs: manger (to eat),
boire (to drink), prendre (to take/have)
